newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila aims 470 bln pesos revenues in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Manila aims 470 bln pesos revenues in 1997.

text.p: The Philippines aims to increase government revenues to 470 billion pesos this year from 1996's forecast 389.5 billion pesos, according to documents issued by the Finance Department on Wednesday.
According to the documents, 95 percent or 447 billion pesos of the projected revenues will come from taxes collected by the Bureau of Internal Revenues (BIR) and the Bureau of Customs (BOC).
The remaining five percent is expected to come from non-tax revenues from the Bureau of Treasury.
The department said the figures were calculated based on exisiting revenue sources and did not take into account any other sources which could come about from fresh legislation.
The state agency forecast an 18.9 percent in revenues of the BIR to 288.5 billion pesos from the past year's 242.6 billion.
Revenues of the BOC are expected to jump by 27.2 percent to 155.3 billion pesos from the projected 122 billion pesos in 1996.

The bulk of the BIR's revenues would come from corporate income taxes at 84 billion pesos, individual income tax at 64.4 billion, and excise taxes on alcoholic and tobacco products, fuels and oils, mining and automobiles at 45 billion pesos

Sales taxes, value added tax, and licenses are seen to contribute another 55.5 billion pesos. This include taxes on banks and financial institutions, insurance premiums, amusement, franchise and stock transactions.
Documentary, property and travel taxes are expected to yield 9.7 billion pesos.
Of the total revenues of the BOC, some 95.5 billion pesos will come from payments of import duties and another 44.7 billion pesos in value added taxes.
